questions.q_en:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

Submit the compliance documents before the deadline expires.
questions.q_hi:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

Submit the compliance documents before the deadline expires.
options_en: The compliance documents are submitted before the deadline expires.
Let the compliance documents be submitted before the deadline expires.
The compliance documents should submitted before the deadline expires.
The compliance documents were submitted before the deadline expires.
options_hi: The compliance documents are submitted before the deadline expires.
Let the compliance documents be submitted before the deadline expires.
The compliance documents should submitted before the deadline expires.
The compliance documents were submitted before the deadline expires.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B)

📌 Rule / Concept: Imperative Sentence in Passive Voice

When an imperative sentence (command/request/order) begins with a base verb, its passive form is generally constructed using:

Let + object + be + V³

Structure:
Active: Verb + object
Passive: Let + object + be + V³

If the imperative is negative, the structure becomes:
Let + object + not be + V³

This structure is standard in formal written English and is frequently tested in SSC and Banking exams.

Here, “Submit” is an imperative verb and “the compliance documents” is the object. To convert into passive, the object becomes the focus, and the structure must follow:

Let + object + be + V³

Therefore, the correct passive form is:
Let the compliance documents be submitted before the deadline expires.

🧠 Things to Remember / Exam Tips

Imperatives always convert using “Let + object + be + V³.” Maintain the command tone. Do not convert it into a simple present statement. Negative imperatives require “not” after the object. This structure is a common direct transformation question in SSC and Banking Mains.

questions.q_en: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
questions.q_hi: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
options_en: The HR manager asked to the candidates
to remain seated in the waiting area
until their respective turns were called.
No Error
options_hi: The HR manager asked to the candidates
to remain seated in the waiting area
until their respective turns were called.
No Error
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A) – Remove TO.

📌Rule/Concept: Direct Objects with Transitive Reporting Verbs -

Certain verbs are transitive, meaning they require a direct object to complete their meaning. The verb 'Ask', when used to mean "requesting someone" or "questioning someone," is a transitive verb. Therefore, it is followed immediately by the person (the object) without the preposition 'to'.

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, "the candidates" is the direct object of the verb "asked." Adding the preposition "to" between a transitive verb and its direct object is a grammatical redundancy. Just as we do not say "He told to me, "we must not say "He asked to me." The preposition "to" is only used with "ask" in very specific, rare idioms (like "ask to see"), but never when placed before the person being addressed

Things to Remember / Exam Tips

The "Tell" Rule: Treat "Ask" like "Tell." You say "Tell him," not "Tell to him." Similarly, use "Ask him," not "Ask to him."

Direct vs. Indirect: "Ask" is followed by the person (Direct Object). The preposition "to" usually appears after the person to introduce the infinitive verb (e.g., Asked him to go).

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1: I asked him to finish the report by Friday afternoon. Example 2: The teacher asked the students to submit their assignments. Example 3: Did you ask the supervisor for permission to leave early?

questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B).

Replace “took your leave” with “took leave of you”

📌 Rule / Concept: Nouns that Reject the Possessive Case -

Certain nouns in English - specifically Leave, Separation, Mention, Report, Sight, Pardon, and Favour—should not be preceded by a possessive adjective (my, your, his, her, their, etc.)

Instead, the relationship must be expressed using a prepositional phrase (usually starting with of or from).

In this sentence, "leave" means the act of departing or bidding farewell. Grammatically, you cannot "possess" the departure of another person in this way.

Corrected Sentence - After the formal conclusion of the meeting, the guest of honor took leave of you and departed for the airport to catch the midnight flight.

More Examples for Clarity -

questions.q_en:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

The central agency will review the compliance framework in the upcoming quarter.
questions.q_hi:
Select the passive form of the given sentence.

The central agency will review the compliance framework in the upcoming quarter.
options_en: The compliance framework will be reviewed by the central agency in the upcoming quarter.
The compliance framework will have been reviewed by the central agency in the upcoming quarter.
The compliance framework is reviewed by the central agency in the upcoming quarter.
The compliance framework will being reviewed by the central agency in the upcoming quarter.
options_hi: The compliance framework will be reviewed by the central agency in the upcoming quarter.
The compliance framework will have been reviewed by the central agency in the upcoming quarter.
The compliance framework is reviewed by the central agency in the upcoming quarter.
The compliance framework will being reviewed by the central agency in the upcoming quarter.
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (A)

📌 Rule / Concept: Simple Future Tense – Active to Passive Conversion

In the Simple Future tense, the active structure is:
Subject + will + V¹ + Object

The passive structure becomes:

Object + will + be + V³ (+ by + Subject)

After “will”, we must use “be” followed by the past participle (V³) of the main verb. The tense must remain future after transformation.

Here, “will review” is in Simple Future tense.
“The compliance framework” is the object and becomes the subject in passive voice. In future passive, we must use “will be” + V³. The verb “review” changes to its past participle form “reviewed”.

Hence, “will be reviewed” is the correct transformation.

The Correct Ans is Option (A)

📌 Rule / Concept: Mixed Conditional (Past Condition → Present Result)

Structure: If + had + V3 (past unreal condition),
would + base verb (present unreal result)

This structure is used when a past action (which did not happen) affects the present situation.

💢 Application to the Given Question - If the compliance team had scrutinised the transaction records more meticulously last quarter…

This clearly refers to a past unreal situation.

the organisation ____ greater regulatory credibility today
and ____ under such intense supervisory pressure at present

The words “today” and “at present” indicate present result.

Therefore, the result clause must use: would + base verb

✅ Corrected Sentence - If the compliance team had scrutinised the transaction records more meticulously last quarter, the organisation would enjoy greater regulatory credibility today and would not be under such intense supervisory pressure at present.

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅ - If the bank had diversified earlier, it would be more stable today.

Example 2 ✅ - If she had accepted the offer, she would be working in London now.

Example 3 ✅ - If the company had invested in technology, it would operate efficiently at present.

questions.q_en: We speculate that repeated testing with this new substance ______ improve the rate of detection.
questions.q_hi: We speculate that repeated testing with this new substance ______ improve the rate of detection.
options_en:
should

would

might

must
options_hi:
should

would

might

must
questions.solution_en:
The Correct Ans is Option (B) - would improve.

📌 Rule / Concept: Conditional Probability vs. Recommendation Modals

This question tests the distinction between:

  • would → hypothetical result / logical expectation
  • should → advice, obligation, or normative judgment

In academic and SSC-style sentences, speculation + expected outcome demands would, not should.

💢 Application to the Given Question

“We speculate that repeated testing with this new substance ___ improve the rate of detection.”

  • “We speculate that…”→ signals uncertainty + hypothesis, not advice
  • The sentence predicts a likely outcome under a hypothetical condition (repeated testing)
  • Therefore, the correct modal is: would improve → expresses expected result

Using should improve would imply:

  • a recommendation, duty, or expectation based on norms
  • which clashes with the verb speculate (non-assertive, non-prescriptive)

questions.solution_en:

📌 Rule/Concept: Stative Verbs and Possession ("Have") -

Verb "have" can be either a stative verb (showing possession/ownership) or an action verb (meaning to eat, drink, or experience something).

When "have" means "to own" or "to possess," it is a stative verb and cannot be used in any continuous form (ing). To show an action that started in the past and continues to the present, we must use the Present Perfect Tense (has/have + V3) instead of the Present Perfect Continuous (has/have + been + V1+ing).

💢 Application to the Given Question - In this sentence, the manager "owns" the car. Since "having" here refers to possession, the Continuous form "has been having" is grammatically incorrect. To fix this, we use the Present Perfect form: "has had." (The first "has" is the auxiliary verb, and "had" is the V3 of "have").

More Examples for Clarity -

Example 1 ✅: I have had this mobile phone for three years. (NOT "I have been having")

Example 2 ✅: She is having lunch right now. (CORRECT because "having" here means "eating"—an action)

Example 3 ✅: They have known each other since childhood. (Stative verb of cognition)

Hang – Hanged – Hanged : Used specifically for capital punishment. This refers to the act of killing a person by suspending them by the neck with a rope.

this Friday, the delegates will discuss
several key climate accords.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is Option (B). Replace “will discuss” with “will have discussed”.

📌 Rule: The Future Perfect "Deadline"

When a sentence uses the phrase "By the time" (or By then, By next week) referring to the future, it establishes a specific deadline. Any action that is expected to be completed before that future deadline must be written in the Future Perfect Tense (will + have + V3).

Future perfect + ‘by the time’ + present indefinite

💢 Application to the Question

In this sentence, we have a fixed point in the future: "This Friday" (when the summit concludes).

  1. The Deadline: The moment the summit concludes (V1 - concludes).

  2. The Action: The discussion of the climate accords.

  3. The Logic: The delegates won't start discussing the accords exactly when the summit ends; the discussion must be finished by that time.

Because the discussion is an "action-to-be-completed" before the end of the summit, the Simple Future ("will discuss") is logically incorrect. It must be shifted to the Future Perfect ("will have discussed").

Corrected Sentence

By the time the global summit concludes this Friday, the delegates will have discussed several key climate accords.

questions.solution_en:

📌 Rule / Concept: Simple Past Tense + Do-Support in Question Tags

When a sentence is in simple past tense and does not contain an auxiliary verb (like was/were/has/have), we use do-support (did/didn’t) in the question tag.

Also, since the statement is positive, the tag must be negative.

💢 Application to the Given Question

  • Main verb: completed (simple past)

  • No auxiliary present

  • So, we use did

  • Statement is positive → tag must be negative

  • Subject “candidates” → plural → they

Therefore: didn’t they?

✅ More Examples for Clarity

Example 1 ✅- They submitted the assignment on time, didn’t they?

Example 2 ✅ - The board approved the proposal, didn’t it?

Example 3 ✅ - The officers inspected the premises, didn’t they?

🧠 Things to Remember

  • Simple past verb → use did/didn’t.

  • No auxiliary in main clause → use do-support.

  • Positive statement → negative tag.

  • Match pronoun with subject number.

questions.q_en:

Many successful leaders often attribute their discipline and determination to the hardships they experienced during childhood.
questions.q_hi:
In the sentence below, identify the type of noun of the word “childhood”:

Many successful leaders often attribute their discipline and determination to the hardships they experienced during childhood.
questions.solution_en:
Answer: C) Abstract Noun

Explanation: An abstract noun refers to an idea, quality, condition, emotion, or state that cannot be seen or touched physically.

Here, “childhood” refers to a stage or condition of life, not to a physical object.

Since it names a state or condition, “childhood” is an abstract noun.
